t: You're on Barry Road, a residential street in East Dulwich, in Southwark. It's named after Charles Barry Junior, the architect, who lived from 1823 to 1900. He was the eldest son of Sir Charles Barry, who designed the Houses of Parliament, and the older brother of the architect Edward Middleton Barry. Barry Junior is best remembered for his work in Dulwich, and for collaborating with Robert Richardson Banks and with his brother Edward on several significant projects. So this quiet street carries the name of the man most associated with this part of south London's architecture.
